subject: Post-call: ACME integration - rate limits, retries, and idempotency
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Lee <amanda@acme.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: ACME integration - rate limits, retries, and idempotency

Hi Amanda / Tom 

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can unblock engineering: 

Summary from our side:
- Goal: Embed Redwood generation + reranker into ACME search flow (query -> embeddings -> rerank -> structured/tool calling for actions).
- Primary constraints: high QPS burst during morning traffic, strict SLA on tail latency (~200ms for first token), and strict audit/ID policies.

Open integration topics we agreed to validate:
1) Auth & SDK setup  API keys + short-lived tokens vs. your platform IAM. We recommended our SDK with optional OAuth integration.
2) Routing & model variants  route high-priority traffic to reserved capacity (Dedicated) or fall back to smaller quantized variants for spikes.
3) Structured outputs / tool-calling  ensure function schemas are validated client-side; we support function-calling with deterministic JSON responses.
4) Rate limiting, quotas, retries, idempotency  most important for you. See details below.

Rate limit guidance (high level):
- Per-tenant quota: 1,200 requests/min (burstable to 2,500 for 30s) for your requested Dedicated profile.
- Token throughput: variable by model; we provide token budgets per-deploy.

Retry and idempotency recommendations (we discussed):
- On 429 (rate-limited): implement exponential backoff with full jitter. Example parameters we recommend: base=500ms, factor=2, max_retries=4, jitter=random(0, base * 2^n).
- Use client-generated request IDs (X-Request-ID or Redwood-Request-Id) on mutating calls to make retries idempotent. We persist recent request IDs for 60s to deduplicate.
- Only retry non-idempotent operations if request ID is present and server indicates safe-to-retry.
- On 5xx (transient server error): short retries (max 2) with exponential backoff; escalate if persistent.

Action items I can take now:
- Attach SDK quickstart and a doc section with ready-made retry/backoff defaults (attached).
- Share a short JSON schema for function-calling and best practices for embedding + reranker batching.

Would you like us to spin up a short-lived sandbox token so your engineers can test the retry behavior against a synthetic traffic pattern? If yes, we can set it up today.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Amanda 

Short answers: yes on OAuth short-lived tokens (we support OIDC/OAuth flows and can map Okta scopes to token scopes).

Batching guidance for embeddings -> rerankers:
- Default: batch size 16 for <= 100ms extra latency. If your p95 latency budget allows, 32-64 will improve throughput but increases tail latency; try 32 as a middle ground.
- Use asynchronous batching in the SDK; we expose maxBatchSize and maxBatchWaitMs.

On 429 handling with upstream gateway: implement cascading/backoff-awareness where your gateway includes its remaining quota headers to clients. Redwood returns standard rate headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset). If both layers return 429, prefer backing off based on the shortest reset window and apply jitter so retries from many clients don't synchronize.

Sandbox token: we can create one scoped to embeddings+rerank for 24 hours and add a test harness for load generation. Tom, Ill create it and send the credentials to your platform mailbox.

Looping in Marissa for pricing/contract alignment if you want longer-term burst increases.

Best,
Ben

Quick engineering note from my side (sending examples you can paste into the SDK config):

- Retry policy (recommended defaults):
  maxRetries = 4
  baseDelayMs = 500
  backoffFactor = 2.0
  useFullJitter = true
  retryOn = [429, 502, 503, 504]
  doNotRetryOn = [400, 401, 403]

- Idempotency: attach header X-Request-ID (UUIDv4) to any create/submit call. Server side will return 409 if duplicate within 60s.

- Example workflow for function-calling + tool: include a call_id in the payload and persist results keyed by call_id so retries return the saved execution instead of invoking the tool twice.

I can drop a tiny test harness and a short runbook for their SREs into the Drive link.

 Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
